title: Stored opposite baseline slopes fail a common-moment test in 49 of 112 selected Allen electrical pairs
abstract: We tested whether opposite baseline slope summaries can share one voltage second-moment matrix in Allen mouse inhibitory electrical pairs. A common matrix requires the same slope sign and a product no greater than one, except when both slopes are zero. Of 112 selected pairs, 43 had opposite signs and six had a product above one. With an assumed absolute error of 0.05 per slope, 38 still failed. In 34 pairs with both pulse p values below 0.05, 18 failed exactly and 14 remained at the 0.05 error limit. We give a sharp error-distance formula and a conditional input-moment inversion. Only one pair passed both single-direction nonnegative-input bounds yet required a negative joint input cross-moment. Separate sweep sets, finite samples and unknown fit errors prevent an inference of a biological state change. This is a check on pooling summaries, not a rejection of passive coupling. Original code, aggregate evidence and external regeneration steps support reproduction. External records are not bundled.
